newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm as foreign buyers enter mkts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm as foreign buyers enter mkts.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed stronger across the board on Tuesday after sustaining initial firmness throughout the session on foreign investors stepping into the local stock and money markets, traders said.
"The peso barely moved all day. The market is waiting for the outcome of (this evening's) Cetes auction," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 0.4 of a centavo firmer at 7.7900/7.7935 and 7.7890/7.7910 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 0.55 centavos firmer at 7.7850/7.7875 per dollar.
"We saw foreign investors step in with the aim of acquiring paper, particularly longer term instruments," another trader said.
Foreign demand for money market instruments could be seen by Overnight rates on Cetes in the secondary money market, which had fallen 40 basis points to 20.00 percent in late trade.
By the same token, foreign buyers boosted the Mexican bourse's blue chip IPC index 1.83 percent to 3,746.62 when the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico.
The amount of foreign capital entering the mexican financial markets also augured falls in primary interest rates, which could weaken the peso, tarders said.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders forecast an average assignment rate of 20.30 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes at the central bank's weekly primary auction. This would be a fall of 115 basis points since last week's auction.
Traders had discounted a fall of up to 50 basis points.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce primary auction results at 1830 local time.
